headline: All majors underwater on the 200-day; shorts liquidating heavily while whales withdraw Bitcoin cold; sentiment fearful but spot ETF bid persists.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguously bearish on structure. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none of them have achieved a golden cross (price above the 50-day, which is above the 200-day). Bitcoin sits 47.8% beneath its 12-month high of $124,739.81; Ethereum is 60.1% down from $4,817.76; Cardano has fallen 79.4% from $0.9631. The crowd is pricing a bear market in structure, not a correction.

Momentum readings present a mixed picture against that downtrend. Bitcoin's RSI-14 is at 56.0 and its MACD is above the signal line, suggesting some upward pressure even while price remains depressed. Solana mirrors this: RSI at 57.7 with MACD above signal. Cardano's RSI has climbed to 66.9 (overbought territory) and MACD is above signal, but price is still $0.198 versus a 12-month high of $0.9631. The tension here is real: momentum indicators are pointing north in a market structure that is still pointing south. When momentum diverges from trend, the first question is whether momentum is leading a reversal or whether the trend reasserts. The fact that price remains well underwater despite overbought or elevated RSI across multiple assets suggests the latter: oversold bounces without conviction.

Funding is moderately elevated but not extreme, and short liquidations dominate. Bitcoin funding is 0.0059% per 8-hour period (6.5% annualized); SOL at 0.0088% per 8-hour (9.6% annualized); XRP and Doge both at 0.01% per 8-hour (11.0% annualized). These are modest rates by historical standards, signaling that longs are not aggressively overpaying to hold. More instructive is the liquidation profile: over the last 19 to 24 hours, shorts have taken far more pain than longs. In Bitcoin, shorts liquidated for $636,350 versus $139,465 for longs. In Ethereum, shorts liquidated $2,684,979 versus $181,797 for longs. In Solana, shorts liquidated $878,345 versus $85,102 for longs. The long-to-short account ratio is elevated across the board (BTC at 1.14, SOL at 2.01, Doge at 4.99), meaning more accounts are positioned long than short. The tape is saying that the market is tilted long structurally, but shorts are getting squeezed in bounce attempts, not blown out in a sustained rally.

Whale behavior is the day's most concrete signal. Over the last 48 hours, Bitcoin has moved off exchanges to the tune of $103,045,101 net outflow. The biggest single moves were withdrawals from Kraken totaling $117,985,783 and $50,072,816. Against that, the biggest inflow was $65,013,498 onto Binance. The weekly net flow history shows extreme volatility: negative $146.9 million, then positive $445.9 million, then a spike to positive $1.075 billion, then back to positive $67.2 million. Large holders are rotating and moving Bitcoin to cold storage or alternative venues while open interest in perpetual futures remains substantial ($2.09 billion on Bitcoin alone at OKX). This is not capitulation; it is consolidation. Whales do not move coins to cold storage when they are ready to dump.

Spot ETF flows remain constructive. Bitcoin ETF saw $101.7 million of inflows on 07 Aug (yesterday by the data date), with all five of the last sessions in the same direction, accumulating $865.3 million over that window. Ethereum ETF added $49.6 million on the same day with four of the last five sessions positive, totaling $243.7 million. The cumulative inflows are substantial: $52.243 billion for Bitcoin, $11.465 billion for Ethereum. Traditional finance has not lost appetite despite the structural bear trend. Stablecoin float sits at $306.23 billion and is down 1.02% over 30 days, a modest decline. The dry powder is still there.

Fear and Greed sits at 31 (Fear) within a 30-day range of 22 to 33. The crowd sentiment is compressed and frightened but not historically extreme; there is lower available. Bitcoin's 7-day change of 0.58% and 30-day change of 8.67% show a slow grind upward off the lows defined by the range (spark low of $58,566.09). The watch is whether momentum can sustain a climb past resistance while the 200-day line remains above price, and whether whale accumulation (inflows to cold storage) continues to absorb selling. A flip in funding direction to shorts paying to hold longs, or a series of days with net inflows onto exchanges after this cold-storage push, would be the signal that the structural bear regime itself is under threat.
